points: Last perek, the potter reshaped the clay: you can still change. Here Yirmiyahu breaks a clay jug in front of the elders: it's too late.
It happens in Gei Ben Hinnom, which you can visit today. The Gemara in Sukkah says the entrance to Gehinnom is there, which is where the name Gehinnom comes from.
The people served Baal and Molech, passing or burning their children, with drums ("tofes") to drown out the screams. The valley will be renamed Gei HaHaregah, the valley of slaughter.
The prophets of Molech claimed Hashem wanted it: sacrifice one child to protect the rest and your wealth. Hashem says, "Asher lo tzivisi," I never commanded this.
Molech's idea lives on when we treat a child as a means to an end, an extension of ourselves to boast about or be ashamed of. Every child must be seen for who they are.
